newsitem.title: INDIA: India Tamil group bombs Russian centre, office.
newsitem.headline: India Tamil group bombs Russian centre, office.

text.p: Tamil extremists exploded two bombs in the southern Indian city of Madras on Monday in apparently synchronised attacks, injuring two people, police said.

The first bomb went off at the Russian Cultural Centre at 3.45 a.m. (2215 GMT Sunday), destroying an air conditioner and shattering window panes in the three-story building. A guard suffered minor injuries.
The second exploded 30 minutes later under a car at the office of the Election Commission, 10 km (six miles) from the Russian Cultural Centre, police said. A sweeper sleeping in the car was injured.

The Tamil Liberation Army, a minor extremist group that sympathises with Tamil separatists in Sri Lanka, claimed responsibility for the attacks in handbills found at both sites in the capital of Tamil Nadu state.
"The sound was deafening and I thought the entire building would come down," one of the security guards at the Russian Cultural Centre said.
Police said they had anticipated violence ahead of celebrations linked to the 50th anniversary of Indian independence on August 15, and have tightened security.
The militant group has a history of setting off explosions during celebrations.
The handbills questioned the need for Independence Day celebrations "when more than half the population remained poor and without a meal".
The militants protested in the handbill against a proposed fast breeder nuclear reactor in Tamil Nadu, police said. The reactor would be built with Russian aid.
Tamil Nadu chief minister M. Karunanidhi urged citizens to cooperate with a police investigation and not to panic.
"The state government will come down heavily upon any group that interferes with the security of the Independence Day celebrations and uses violence," Karunanidhi said.
Former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was killed by a suicide bomber from a Tamil militant group in Tamil Nadu state in 1991.
